content:
Stephanie Nguyen: Sharing a couple early replies from outbound this morning — benchmark is definitely getting read.

- Prospect (devtools): “Numbers look strong. Can you share exactly how to reproduce the latency/$ figure in our own PoC? We don’t want a marketing benchmark.”
- Prospect (fintech): “What prompt set + concurrency did you use? If we run this ourselves will we see similar p95?”

AEs are asking for a simple “how to replicate” guide we can send w/o dragging eng into every thread. Do we have something ready?

Markus Klein: +1, SE team is getting the same. We need a short doc we can attach that:
1) points to public methodology
2) tells them what they can realistically replicate (and what they can’t)
3) gives a quick recipe to run a comparable test on their own prompts

Also: what’s the safe answer if they ask “did you enable caching?”

Lukas Meyer: EMEA angle: prospects are asking specifically “which EU region did you measure” + “can we run it in eu-central for data residency”. If we can include region pinning steps in the guide that would help.

Soojin Lee: We don’t have a single packaged “replication” handout yet (we have methodology + internal runbook). Let’s create a PoC-friendly version that’s safe to share.

Constraints from Legal: don’t promise they’ll get the same numbers; we can say “you can reproduce the methodology and compare relative performance across models/regions under similar workload conditions.”

Claire Dubois: Re caching: published headline numbers were run with the benchmark harness configured to avoid cross-request caching effects (no shared prefix cache across independent requests). We do warmup runs to stabilize kernel selection + KV allocation, but the measured window is steady-state.

We should phrase it like:
- “We ran with a consistent batching policy across all models/regions.”
- “We did not rely on application-specific prompt caching.”

If they want to test their own app, we *recommend* trying caching/batching later because that’s how production systems get cheaper — but that’s a separate optimization pass.

Rina Kobayashi: For a “replicate it” recipe, we can give them the docker runner path (the one we used internally is basically the same now).

Something like:

```
# prereqs: docker + a Redwood API key
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...

docker run --rm \
  -e REDWOOD_API_KEY \
  ghcr.io/redwood-inference/benchmark-runner:2025.07.09 \
  region-sweep \
  --model <model_id> \
  --region <region> \
  --prompt-set production-mix-v3 \
  --concurrency 1,4,16 \
  --prefill-tokens 1024 \
  --decode-tokens 256 \
  --streaming false \
  --runs 5 \
  --output results.json
```

And then link them to the metric definitions (latency/$, p50/p95, $/1M tokens) + note on variance.

We should sanity-check the exact flags we want to expose so we don’t create 10 variants.

Jonas Weber: Agree. The key is giving them a “close enough” reproducible path.

What we should *not* do:
- share any internal fleet sizing / capacity reservation steps
- share raw internal run manifests that might reveal infra details

What we *can* do:
- runner + public prompt set id
- model version pin (if available) and region pin
- warmup + measured window guidance
- recommend they run on their own prompts too (that’s the real PoC)

Elliot Price: I can draft a 1–2 pager today and we can host it in docs as “Reproducing the Benchmark in a PoC” and link it from the FAQ.

Proposed structure:
1) What you can replicate (methodology + harness)
2) What will differ (prompt mix, context length distribution, region capacity, customer-side network, streaming)
3) Step-by-step quickstart (docker + CLI)
4) How to interpret results (variance, p95 vs throughput)
5) When to talk to us (Dedicated sizing, Private/VPC, custom workloads)

Renee Sullivan: Please include copy for the “prospect asks for exact number match” scenario. Something like:
“Benchmarks are a snapshot under a defined workload. If your traffic pattern differs (longer contexts, streaming, tool calls, different concurrency), your absolute numbers will vary — the right PoC is to run the same harness on *your* prompt set and compare tradeoffs.”

Also suggest a template email snippet for AEs.

Markus Klein: +1 on email snippet. For SEs, we also need a 30-second talk track:
- “Here’s the harness and prompt set.”
- “Pin model+region.”
- “Run 3 concurrencies.”
- “Compare p95 and cost per 1M.”

And a line about why we focus on latency/$ vs tokens/sec.

Claire Dubois: On region pinning: include explicit examples like `us-east`, `eu-west`, `apac-sg` (whatever the marketing page lists as supported). And a note: “If you need eu-central specifically for residency, we can do Dedicated/Private in-region; Hosted availability may vary.” (wordsmithing needed).

Soojin Lee: Action items:
- Elliot draft the external-facing “how to replicate” guide (today)
- Rina/Claire review the exact command/flags + safe wording re: caching/batching (tomorrow AM)
- Markus + Stephanie: provide 3 real prospect questions you want answered verbatim so we cover them

Once it’s in docs, we’ll share a shortlink in #sales and add it to the enablement kit.

Stephanie Nguyen: Perfect. I’ll drop prospect Qs here:
1) “Did you use speculative decoding / any special tricks?”
2) “Can we reproduce on our AWS region?”
3) “If we run it at concurrency=50 will it look the same?”

Markus Klein: Adding another common one: “Is this with streaming on? Our app streams tokens.”

Jonas Weber: We should answer those explicitly:
- Spec decoding: “not required for the benchmark; if enabled, disclosed per model/config” (keep it factual)
- Region: “use the regions in our published list; other regions are available on request via Dedicated/Private”
- Concurrency: “higher concurrency changes queueing; run a sweep and look at p95 + error rates; don’t extrapolate from a single point”
- Streaming: “streaming changes perceived latency; we report non-streaming end-to-end completion by default; streaming-specific metrics may differ”

Elliot Price: Got it. I’ll draft and share a link for review in this thread.

Lukas Meyer: Thank you — once we have it, I’ll translate the region language into an EMEA-safe snippet (no overpromises on residency).

Soojin Lee: Cool. Let’s aim to have the shareable doc ready before tomorrow’s outbound block.
